Consultant agrees to act as a consultant to Company with respect to such matters and projects as are mutually agreed from time to time by and between Consultant and Company, and perform the services described on Exhibit A hereto (collectively, "Services").

reviews.rationale: The clause is a payment_terms provision that ties Consultant's compensation to Exhibit A, which is not provided. None of the retrieved positions squarely govern this obligation: no-minimum-commitment concerns a customer's absence of purchase/volume commitments, and revenue-share-defined concerns calculation, capping and auditability of a revenue/profit share. reviews.rationale: The clause imposes a one-way confidentiality obligation on Consultant only, while the relevant preferred position (confidentiality-mutual) contemplates mutual obligations between the parties. It also includes the standard exclusions for prior knowledge, public availability, and third-party receipt, which is consistent with the preferred position. However, the clause lacks a time limit on the confidentiality obligation, creating indefinite residual exposure; the confidentiality-term preferred position limits survival to three years (five in fallback), with indefinite duration only for trade secrets. The deviation is a negotiable gap rather than a prohibition breach, so it is assessed as medium.

These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to it, or is independently developed by it.

The confidentiality obligations in this Agreement survive for three (3) years after termination or expiry, and indefinitely with respect to trade secrets for so long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

reviews.suggested_fallback: The confidentiality obligations in this Agreement survive for five (5) years after termination or expiry, and indefinitely with respect to trade secrets for so long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

The clause indeed imposes one-way confidentiality obligations on Consultant only, and the cited confidentiality-mutual preferred position contemplates mutual obligations, so the noted deviation is accurate. The rationale distinguishes what the clause states from what policy requests, and the medium risk level reasonably follows from a negotiable gap rather than a prohibition breach. clause.heading: 3. Ownership. Consultant hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest in and to any information (including, without limitation, business plans and/or business information), technology, know-how, materials, notes, records, designs, ideas, inventions, improvements, devices, developments, discoveries, compositions, trade secrets, processes, methods and/or techniques, whether or not patentable or copyrightable, that are conceived, reduced to practice or made by Consultant alone or jointly with others in the course of performing the Services or through the use of Confidential Information (collectively, 111nventions").

reviews.rationale: The clause is a broad assignment of all Inventions to Company made in the course of the Services or through use of Confidential Information. The only retained Consultant right is an implied-in-fact fallback: the non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual license to Items owned by Consultant that are incorporated into an Invention. This is not 'background IP retention' as required by the cited position; the clause lacks a provision preserving ownership of Consultant's pre-existing or independently developed IP, so the playbook's stated trigger ('Risk if absent: high') applies.

citations.excerpt: Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it. Ownership of intellectual property created specifically for Customer under a Statement of Work transfers to Customer on payment in full.

reviews.verification_reason: The high risk level and the core 'absent background IP retention' rationale are supported: the clause broadly assigns all Inventions and contains no provision preserving Consultant's pre-existing or independently developed IP, so the cited position's trigger applies. However, the rationale mischaracterizes the Items provision as an 'implied-in-fact fallback' and a 'retained Consultant right.' The clause instead grants Company a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide license to exploit Consultant-owned Items incorporated into an Invention — this is a license granted to Company, not a retained right in Consultant's background IP, and it is express rather than implied. The clause also requires Consultant to disclose such incorporated Items in writing. This correction is needed because the rationale materially misstates the contract text, even though the overall risk level remains supportable under the cited playbook position.

The clause also lacks the policy's 'without penalty or further liability other than amounts accrued' formulation and affirmatively continues payment obligations and survival provisions (Sections 2, 3, 5(c), 6, 7, 8, 10), so it does not cleanly track the policy's liability cap; this is residual exposure rather than a prohibition breach. No assignment, renewal, cure-period, or audit obligations appear in the clause, so those positions are not applied.

The clause covers legal compliance in a targeted way and imposes only a notification duty, not an unrelated restriction. reviews.rationale: The clause imposes a one-way, open-ended non-compete on Consultant: it bars Consultant from participating in any business in the Field of Interest or otherwise competitive with the Company during the entire Term, with no time, territory, or service-scope limitation. This materially deviates from the bounded non-compete position, which permits restrictions only for 12 months post-termination, limited to the territory of actual performance and to services directly competing with those supplied under the Agreement. Because the restriction is not bounded and contains no post-term limit, it breaches the cited policy and exposes the counterparty to broad, indefinite restraint.

The reviewer correctly states the policy preference in the negative and accurately describes the fallback as requiring 12 months post-termination, territory of actual performance, and direct competitive services. The suggested fallback matches the playbook fallback verbatim. The high risk level follows from the absence of any bounded non-compete terms and the explicit high risk if absent. The rationale distinguishes the clause's actual terms from the policy's requested bounds, though its statement that the clause 'contains no post-term limit' is imprecise because the clause only applies 'during the term' and thus does not purport to impose a post-term restriction at all; this does not undermine the grounding or the risk level.
